image: A relief-aid porter bent under a tall, tightly-stacked bundle of donated clothes and crates, straps crossing his chest and splayed legs braced beneath the load — the helper hauling everything at once.
A square, mirror-still marsh pool at the foot of two grassy slopes that fan open above it, clumps of reed poking up from its rim.
A clawed hand descending from above to clamp the narrow neck of a bulging earthen pitcher, three fingers splayed over its rounded shoulders.
A flea-market haggler braced on two planted legs, mouth flung wide mid-shout, tossing two coins spinning up into the air above his head to seal a trade.
Two small wooden thread-bobbins hung side by side beneath a short splayed crossbar, each wound with a tiny coil of floss dangling a loose end.
A cupped hand curling down and around to scoop up a small heap of loose rice grains, fingers wrapping the pile against the palm.
A bent arm curled all the way around a wet, freshly-thrown clay pot, hugging it against the body on the way to the kiln.
A swift folded into a steep dive, wings swept back into one blurred hook, a cross of motion-lines slashing the air behind it.
A green buck-private snapping a stiff salute with one sharply bent arm, a cross-strap bandolier slung over his chest.
A bare, muscled forearm cocked sharply back at the elbow, the fist curled into a tight knot below the swept diagonal line of the upper arm.
A gloved hand slips out from beneath a two-shelved stone overhang on the left, palming a counterfeit seal it has just swapped for the genuine one — caught mid-fake.
A sweeping tiled pagoda eave shades a courtier who thrusts a brush-scepter straight up and bellows a proclamation from a wide-open mouth below — all the swagger of the Tang court.
A stout stake driven into the earth, crossed by three iron bars and capped with a sharp peaked ferrule, planted at an angle to brace against and hold back a charge.
A young horse caught mid-prance — head tossed back in a tight curl, forelegs splayed wide, hind legs planted, one rear hoof trailing behind in the dust.
A fat terrapin plodding at its own lazy pace, its cross-marked domed shell riding high, four stubby legs splayed out, one hind foot dragging a slow trail behind it.

An enormous pleated prize rosette pinned to a puffed-out chest, its spread ribbon-star flaring wide across the top and two flat award-ribbons crossing below into one long curling tail — worn purely to brag.
A bound servant led on a short cord — a clawed hand at the top gripping the leash, a thread trailing down to a large splay-limbed figure below.
A canvas hammock slung low and sagging into a soft cross of woven cord, the midday sun a bright square hanging directly above it — the very picture of a balmy, do-nothing afternoon.
A tall three-tiered kiln — domed cap, glowing stoke-mouth, and a small stoker crouched at its foot — with one round clay pot just tonged out the side to judge which piece has fired ripe.
A lean serpent coiled up in the rafters just under a steep peaked roof, its hooked tail curling down from the eaves — the other resident of the house, the one that isn't you.
A little log cabin with a steep peaked roof buried under heavy snow, drifts piled to the windowsills, every sound swallowed so the woods around it stand dead silent.
A fencer frozen mid-lunge, back leg thrown out in one long curving sweep, a single dark mole marking the raised shoulder — the standout swordsman, a cut above the rest.
A flat-topped hill ringed with squared stone battlements, a jagged rock peak jutting up from inside the encircling walls — a fortified ridge held to the last.
Three thin rivulets snaking straight down a muddy bank side by side, their surfaces rippling and glinting — the raw 'river' radical, water on the move.
Three straight channels of water plunging down through a flat stone lid into a pillared conduit below — hidden streams sluicing along underground, unseen but always flowing.
A heavy iron staple, its flat crossbar pressed down and two stout prongs biting into a plank — as if two iron tens were hammered flat and fused into a single bar.
A moth-eaten battle banner hanging in shreds, a stick rapping it from the right so loose threads scatter into the air — cloth beaten until it is threadbare and ragged.
A wooden execution cart rolled into the square, a broad headsman's axe propped against its right wheel — the blade that ends the condemned with a single slashing stroke.
A hooded figure wrapped in a cloak, bent forward and flinging open a squared shouting mouth — the eternal questioner heckling 'why?! how?!' from under his hood.
A slender hand slowly drawing a long, gauzy veil down across one wide staring eye, the silk stretched out gracefully — beauty pulled out long and wide.
A low tabletop built from three flat wooden slats laid side by side across a single stout tree-trunk leg, the boards still rough and unplaned.
A bare footprint pressed deep into wet sand with a small bent iron hook lying flush against its right edge, the pair jabbed down to mark 'this exact spot.'
A squat brick kiln with four tongues of flame licking along its base and a fat plume of black smoke curling up out of the slot on top.
A hand reaches straight down from above to press a short rod into a waiting open hand below, the baton caught crossways between them mid-pass.
Two pairs of pale reed strands crossed over one another into a tight double-X weave, the first courses of a woven basket wall.
A single curved ivory tusk jutting up from a boar's jaw, a deep interlocking notch cut where it once ground against its opposite fang.
A young cow lifting its head to bellow, a small curl of warm breath puffing up off the top of its snout as the 'moo' escapes.
A round gourd hanging from a curling vine, two thin tendrils splaying out to either side to cradle it as it sways.
A single eye stretched fully round and staring, a bright ring of iris circling the fixed pupil, set just above the draped collar of a loose robe.
A crouching beast's hindquarters drawn in tight, its tail curled under and hooking around inside a low three-walled pen, pressing a rounded track into the dirt.
A horned griffin thrashing inside a box-trap — a single spike of horn jutting up through the peaked lid, its clawed hindquarters and long tail curling out and hooking off the bottom-right corner.
A pointed-roof granary — a square strongbox capped by a peaked lid — perched atop a single drooping rice stalk, its little door swung open as measured grain is doled out as wages.
A pale ball of foxfire, a four-pointed spark of cold green light, hovering just above two skeletal feet splayed apart mid-stride, drifting over a black midnight marsh.
A flat upper lip forming the top bar, from which a squared jaw-curtain hangs, four stiff grey whiskers dangling straight down inside it — a beard combed into rigid parallel strands.
A heavy stone basin whose inner walls are scored with two facing rows of grinding teeth, a stubby pestle standing upright in the hollow and rice husks scattered around the rim.
A dense sheaf of upright thorny stalks bristling into a spiked crown at the top, hoisted from below by two braced hands, prickers jutting out in every direction.
A bare hand closing gently around a short-tailed fledgling lifted out of a tuft of grass, the fingers weighing the little bird as if gauging its size.
A wide kimono sleeve held open to reveal a hidden inner pocket, a folded letter and a single tear-brimmed eye tucked deep in the pressed folds of the robe.
A taut war-drum mounted on a tall footed pedestal and crowned with a spiky, mountain-shaped finial, booming so loud that onlookers gasp and jump back.
A long-bodied marten frozen mid-pounce, its small whiskered head lifted, spine arched high, and its long tail sweeping down to hook sharply to the right.
A squat iron money-chest with a fat cowrie-shell clasp on its front, its flat lid heaped with three sprays of cut wildflowers spilling over the edges — plain treasure dressed up to be shown off.

A standing figure seen in strict profile, spine held straight but the belly bowed out in one heavy pregnant curve, a single hand resting on the swell — the whole body reduced to that outward-bulging line.
A robed magistrate on the right grips a glowing needle-tipped branding iron and presses it toward a prisoner who kneels open-mouthed at the left, meting out the searing mark of the law.
A lone porter strides along a winding dirt road, a fresh slab of meat hoisted flat on one upturned hand above his shoulder — a traveler hauling his single possession down the trail.
A tall castle gateway with a slatted wooden lattice-grille half-lowered between its two door-posts, the crossed bars bundled tight across the threshold to bar the way.
A plump grey wild goose in gliding profile, neck outstretched and honking, wings spread as it skims just beneath the overhanging lip of a jutting cliff ledge.
A squat bronze ritual cauldron standing on three hollow, splayed legs, a domed lid clamped over its bulging body and a thin thread of steam curling up from the seam.
A heavy grain-head of millet bent over on its stalk, the loaded panicle nodding down toward a trickle of water pooled beneath it.
